entries.name: William Z. Foster

expected_cases.charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government
expected_cases.convicted: Indicted 1948; case severed for ill health; never tried
expected_cases.sentence:
Under indictment (severed); not tried

Note on the arrest date stored on this row. March 6, 1930 is the date of the New York unemployment demonstration at Union Square, more than eighteen years before the Smith Act indictment; it cannot be the arrest for this case. It is left in place rather than deleted because it appears to be a real datum attached to the wrong row, and the 1930 prosecution — for which Foster did serve time — has no record of its own. Worth giving one.

expected_cases.charges: Arrested in the Industrial Workers of the World free-speech fight at Spokane, Washington, 1909-1910.
expected_cases.sentence:
Forty-seven days in the Spokane City Jail, during the IWW free-speech fight of 1909-1910. This is the longest term Foster is recorded as actually serving.

No dates are entered, and so no imprisonment counter is produced from this row. The forty-seven days are documented but its endpoints are not, and the schema records a documented duration in months (imprisoned_for_months), not in days — a documented day-count with unknown endpoints has nowhere to go. Recorded here in the text so the fact is not lost.

expected_cases.charges: Michigan Criminal Syndicalism Act — attending the underground Communist Party convention at Bridgman, Michigan, raided by federal and state authorities on August 22, 1922.
expected_cases.convicted: No — the 1923 trial ended in a hung jury, divided six to six after more than thirty-one hours
expected_cases.sentence:
No conviction and no sentence. Foster was arrested at Chicago on August 22, 1922 and was the first Communist leader brought to trial after the Bridgman raid; the jury hung six to six in 1923 and he served nothing on the charge.

No custody dates are entered. He was arrested and prosecuted, and the length of any pretrial detention is not established, so this row carries no imprisonment figure. It is here because the database records politically motivated arrests and prosecutions that end without conviction, not only completed sentences.

updates.charges: Prosecution arising from the March 6, 1930 unemployment demonstration in New York City
updates.sentence: Contemporary reporting documents six months actually spent in jail for leading the March 6, 1930 unemployment demonstration, followed by release on October 21, 1930. Admission date remains unverified. This separate episode does not duplicate the later Smith Act prosecution.

entries.rationale: Original Laisve November 3 1930 page 5 visually verified: explicit actual release October 21 and six months in jail. Preserve all three existing cases; the later Smith Act row mistakenly carries the March 6 action date but contains no custody span or documented total, so this new documented-month term does not double-count a prior counter. Do not derive admission from six months or treat action date as admission.
